reading.body:
New York has exactly one data center with a published power figure, and it is 3 MW, which is too small to train a frontier model.

The pattern is disclosure, not capacity. Thirty-one data center locations are mapped in New York, and CyrusOne's Wappingers Falls campus is the only one whose operator publishes an IT capacity number. A single published figure cannot describe a state's data center portfolio, and the data does not claim it does. What it establishes is that the public record on New York AI compute is close to empty.

The 3 MW matters because of what it cannot do. At a conservative 30 kW per rack, the 100,000 square feet of technical space works out to roughly 100 racks. A modern GPU cluster draws 50 to 100 MW. This facility is regional colocation, and it cannot host a large training run or inference cluster on its own. Its SSAE 16 Type II certification makes it eligible for audited workloads, which is a compliance fact rather than a compute fact.

The limits are worth stating plainly. The data covers one campus, one operator, and one certification. It says nothing about the other 30 mapped New York locations, nothing about power actually available at the site, and nothing about expansion. The suitability score of 46 is a weighted mean of published inputs, and the missing input is announced expansion. Read the 3 MW as the size of the published record in New York, not the size of New York's compute.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
